android.head: Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing.
android.body: App Total New Subs is -29.3% while App Total Install is -0.4% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-29.0pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is +3.5% right now, so expect that to cool off.

android.head: App Total Revenue +3.5% does not match new subs -32.5% from 7 days earlier — this growth is not coming from new customers.
android.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is +3.5%, but App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -32.5% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

android.head: App Total New Subs is moving slower than the other steps (-29.3% vs about -0.6%).
android.body: App Total New Subs is -29.3% while the other steps are all moving about -0.6% — a gap of -28.7pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

ios.head: App Total Install -5.2% — Organic Install is behind most of it (-9,029, -8.5%).
ios.body: App Total Install was 206,658, against 218,010 for last week — a change of -11,352. Where that came from: Organic Install -9,029 (-8.5%), Paid Install -1,500 (-1.6%), SEO Install -972 (-6.0%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (-9,029, -8.5%) and is now 46.8% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

ios.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCP New Subs -6.2% vs Install -12.3% (better than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

ios.head: App Total Install -5.2% is mostly YCP — not every app.
ios.body: App Total Install moved -5.2% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -5.2%, YMK -1.2%, YCP -12.3%, YCV -1.3%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

ios.head: US is out of line with every other country on App Total Install (-0.1% vs -5.2%).
ios.body: For All App, App Total Install in US is -0.1% while all countries together are -5.2% — a gap of +5.1pp. US is about 37% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

ios.head: GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (24.1% vs 12.8% overall).
ios.body: In GB, 24.1% of installs turn into new subs, versus 12.8% across all markets and apps (+11.3pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 5% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -7.8% this period.

ios.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is -4.4% and App Total Install is -5.2%; the gap between them (+0.8pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
